messages:
sara: Hey @pete — customer reports their SSE chat stream pauses ~1.2s mid-message, then final tokens arrive concatenated. Started after an edge config push.
pete: Can you grab a request id from the failing session?
customer-ops: req_9a8b7c6d routed via Fastly, edge-id=res_73f1, ts=2026-11-04T18:12:07Z
sara: OK thanks. Can you run this curl from the customer host and paste full verbose output?

curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/streams\" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"stream":true}'

pete: While they're at it, capture a short pcap: `sudo tcpdump -w sse-issue.pcap -s 0 port 443 and host api.redwood.ai` — we want to see packet timing and delayed ACKs.
arjun: Quick checklist: client runtime (browser/node), HTTP client lib/version, OS, NAT/proxy between client and edge, and whether TLS terminates at edge.
sara: Hypothesis: edge coalescing + client TCP Nagle + gzip/coalesce on Fastly causing flush delays. Can we confirm content-length/chunking? customer-ops please share the raw request/response headers from curl.
customer-ops: Headers show `transfer-encoding: chunked` from worker -> edge, but Fastly inserted gzip and set `accept-encoding: gzip` upstream. Also observed small pauses in packets matching the timeline.
sara: Please try this minimal node repro (so we can rule out browser buffering):

node -e "const r=require('node-fetch'); r('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/streams',{headers:{'accept':'text/event-stream','authorization':'Bearer ...'}, method:'POST',body:JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-3b',messages:[{role:'user',content:'x'.repeat(5000)}],stream:true})}).then(res=>{res.body.on('data',d=>console.log('chunk',d.length))})"

pete: Also useful: run `curl --no-buffer` and `curl -v --raw` to see if libcurl is coalescing. For browsers, adding `responseType: 'stream'` and disabling compression on the edge helps isolate.
arjun: I collected worker logs for res_73f1: repeated log lines `flush_pending=false` around the pause; the worker did not emit events, it appears the edge buffered ~16KB before flush.
sara: Customer, please upload a debug bundle (curl + tcpdump + system info) to this link: https://dl.redwood/debug-bundles/upload/req_9a8b7c6d and reply here when done.
customer-ops: Uploaded -> https://dl.redwood/debug/req_9a8b7c6d.tar.gz
arjun: Downloaded bundle. I can see the pcap: bursts of TLS records then a 1.2s gap. Edge is sending back combined SSE frames after gap. Worker-side events look fine and are emitted in small chunks.
pete: Next actions: 1) Eng-infra to check Fastly VCL for gzip/coalesce thresholds; suggest immediate test toggling `gzip` and `streaming` behavior. 2) Ask customer to disable TCP_NODELAY? actually enable TCP_NODELAY to avoid Nagle on their side, and try `--no-buffer` curl. 3) We'll run a canary with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` + flush-on-write on a test host.
eng-infra-bot: Ticket INF-4123 created and linked to request res_73f1 (assigned to eng-infra).
sara: Thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated with the curl + pcap ask and link the debug bundle into the eng-infra ticket. :thumbsup:
